chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan al-Jammal said:
I prayed behind Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) for several days, and he would perform Qunut in every prayer, whether it was recited aloud or silently.
ai.seo_question: Did the Imams perform Qunut in both loud and silent prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted via Safwan al-Jammal, establishes the consistency of Qunut in both Fajr and other prayers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imams' precise adherence to ritual etiquette. It highlights the theological significance of Qunut not merely as a supplication but as an integral component of the prayer structure, distinguishing Shia practice from other schools that may limit it to Fajr or specific occasions. The hadith underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition through the Imams, reinforcing the authority of their practical demonstrations (Sunnah) in legal jurisprudence.
